rows.stage: Land — first glance at the README
rows.visitor: A first-time visitor who clicked a link. They will spend seconds, scanning the top of the README to decide whether to keep reading at all.
rows.job: In one glance, understand what fak is and see that it does something real — an identity line, a headline number, a runnable first command visible above the fold.

tokens: fast, enforceable boundary between your agent and every tool call
affordances.need: a one-sentence 'what fak is' the visitor can grasp in a glance, near the top of the README (the current front-door line: 'One binary puts a fast, enforceable boundary between your agent and every tool call')
a copy-pasteable hero command in a fenced block, so the visitor sees a runnable first move without scrolling
the honest headline benchmark numbers on the front page — measured decode tok/s per hardware family, each with claim boundaries beside it and a receipt link (the #9751 latest-hardware front page)
the headline number is anchored to a source (benchmark authority + the honesty ledger) so it reads as real, not marketing
a hero visual the front page can lead with — one picture/video that makes the win legible in seconds

gaps: The hero is a benchmark video + numbers; an interactive in-browser demo would convert an even-lower-effort visitor

rows.stage: Orient — the five concepts, named and reachable
rows.visitor: A visitor who is intrigued and now wants the mental model: what are the actual ideas here, and can I get them from one page?
rows.job: Find the five core concepts named in plain language, each reachable from a front-door surface — so the visitor can re-explain fak to a colleague a week later.

affordances.need: the five core concepts named together on a reader-facing surface (syscall model, verify-don't-trust, addressable KV cache, default-deny capability gate, single-binary drop-in)
the flagship 'treat the tool call like a syscall' explainer — the one-page read that makes the whole design click
a concept glossary that gives each idea one canonical name and definition
the machine-readable doc-map (llms.txt) so an answer engine can orient a visitor who asks it about fak
a docs map on the README that routes 'if you want X, read Y' — so orienting is one hop, not a search
an ordered concept path for a visitor who wants to learn the ideas in sequence

gaps: The five concepts are named on concepts-and-story.md and the epic doc; a single-screen 'concept card' image would make them even more repeatable
